label: sec:mass-algebraic-consolidated-intro
html:
With the Wedderburn decomposition and the Hoefsmit seminormal basis in place, the mass functional reduces to explicit operator evaluations on braid words. This section develops the three algebraic pillars of that evaluation:

  1. Transfer-matrix factorisation and skein mass: The transfer-matrix operator propagates crossing weights along a closed braid so that the skein polynomial and the \beta-decay transition amplitude factor as matrix products, reducing composite link masses to linking numbers plus hyperbolic volume increments; on the Borromean nucleon the pair-skein mass formula gives the nucleon mass and the proton–neutron flavor split.
  2. Two-row Markov corrections and the Temperley–Lieb radical: Under the canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the three-strand antisymmetriser weight y_{(1^3)} vanishes identically. The radical of the Markov Gram pairing G on H_n(q) coincides with the kernel of the Temperley–Lieb quotient H_n(q) \twoheadrightarrow \mathrm{TL}_n(q), so G descends to a positive-definite sesquilinear form on \mathrm{TL}_n(q) while blocking any naive unquotiented Connes distance.
  3. Bi-filtration and the adelic substrate: The Lusztig bar involution and the Hermitian star involution induce a joint cellular-depth and jet-degree bi-filtration on H_n(q), conjecturally stratified by the curvature rank of the Hecke curvature 2-cocycle, linking the algebraic substrate to its archimedean realization \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}.
